name: Wachau
summary: A narrow stretch of the Danube valley with hot, dry summers and cold winters. Dry stone terraces on weathered gneiss, with loess in places, carry mostly Grüner Veltliner and Riesling, made as dry whites.
label_note: Wachau DAC has three origin levels: Gebietswein (regional, 17 permitted varieties), Ortswein (a named village or the Großlage Spitzer Graben, nine white varieties) and Riedenwein (a single vineyard, Grüner Veltliner or Riesling only, no chaptalisation). Grapes must be hand picked and the vintage is mandatory.

name: Kremstal
summary: Vineyards around the town of Krems on the Danube. Weathered primary rock in the north suits Riesling, while the loess terraces east of the town give a rounder Grüner Veltliner. Both are the grapes of Kremstal DAC.
label_note: Kremstal DAC is Grüner Veltliner or Riesling, dry, with the vintage on the label. It may name a village from the annex (Ortsangabe) or a Ried, and Kremstal DAC Reserve (at least 13.0% vol) is a fuller style in which slight botrytis and oak are allowed.

name: Kamptal
summary: The valley of the river Kamp around Langenlois, north of the Danube. Loess, gravel and very old primary rock soils, as on the Heiligenstein hill, carry the two main grapes, Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
label_note: Kamptal DAC has three levels: Gebietswein, Ortswein (one of 12 cross-village wine communes listed in the annex) and Riedenwein. Permitted grapes are Grüner Veltliner, Riesling, Chardonnay, Weißburgunder and Grauburgunder. From the 2025 harvest the grapes must be certified organic or Nachhaltig Austria, with small-producer exceptions.

name: Wagram
summary: A long terrace of deep loess above the north bank of the Danube, plus the vineyards around Klosterneuburg south of the river. The loess gives full, flavoursome whites led by Grüner Veltliner; Zweigelt is the main red.
label_note: Wagram DAC is dry and carries the vintage. Gebietswein may use 13 varieties; Ortswein (named Katastralgemeinden only) seven single varieties; Riedenwein only Grüner Veltliner, Roter Veltliner or Riesling.

name: Weinviertel
summary: Austria's largest wine region, covering the north east of Lower Austria. Its flagship is Grüner Veltliner: Weinviertel DAC is dry, fruity and spicy with a peppery note, without oak or botrytis.
pairing: Wiener Schnitzel and spicy Asian or vegetarian dishes.
label_note: Weinviertel DAC is Grüner Veltliner only, with at most 6 g/l residual sugar, no oak and no botrytis, and the vintage on the label. Weinviertel DAC Reserve (at least 13.0% vol) and Große Reserve are fuller styles; a village, Großlage or Ried may be named.

grapes.local_note: Fruity and spicy, with a peppery note.

appellations.name: Weinviertel DAC
appellations.note: Grüner Veltliner; fruity, spicy, peppery, no oak.

name: Leithaberg
summary: Between the Leitha hills and Lake Neusiedl, which tempers the climate. Leitha limestone and mica schist give tight, mineral wines: red Blaufränkisch, and whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay and Grüner Veltliner.
label_note: Leithaberg DAC red must be Blaufränkisch; white must be Weißer Burgunder, Chardonnay, Neuburger, Grüner Veltliner or a blend of them. Both must be dry (reds below 2.5 g/l sugar) and may be Gebietswein or, with a narrower origin, Ortswein or Riedenwein.

grapes.local_note: The grape of red Leithaberg DAC.

appellations.note: Weißer Burgunder, Chardonnay, Neuburger, Grüner Veltliner or a blend.

name: Neusiedlersee
summary: East of Lake Neusiedl, with hot, dry summers and little rain. The lake moderates temperatures and its autumn mists bring noble rot. Fruity Zweigelt leads the reds, alongside sweet wines from white grapes.
label_note: Neusiedlersee DAC has four categories: Zweigelt (fruity, spicy, at most 4 g/l sugar, no Ried name), Zweigelt Reserve (aged in large casks or barrique, at least 13.0% vol), fruity sweet Spätlese or Auslese from white grapes, and nobly sweet Beerenauslese or Trockenbeerenauslese as Reserve. Sweet wines from Apetlon, Illmitz or Podersdorf may add „Seewinkel“.

name: Südsteiermark
summary: Steep hills on the southern edge of the Graz basin, on sand, slate, marl and limestone. Warm days and cool nights give a long season and crisp, aromatic whites, led by Sauvignon Blanc.
label_note: Südsteiermark DAC is white only, from hand-picked grapes of eight varieties, at most 4 g/l sugar, with the vintage on the label. It has three levels: Gebietswein, Ortswein (Kitzeck-Sausal, Eichberg, Leutschach, Gamlitz or Ehrenhausen, each with set lead varieties) and Riedenwein.
